title: One case per item
starter:
let price item =
  match item with
  | "milk" -> 3
  | _ -> 0
hints: Each case is one line: a bar, the value to compare with, an arrow, the answer. Copy the `"milk"` line and change it.
The new cases must go above `| _ -> 0`. OCaml tries cases from the top, and `_` fits everything.
`| "eggs" -> 4` and `| "bread" -> 5`, both between the `"milk"` line and the `_` line.

answer.code:
let price item =
  match item with
  | "milk" -> 3
  | "eggs" -> 4
  | "bread" -> 5
  | _ -> 0
answer.explain: `match` compares `item` with each case from the top and uses the first one that fits. Three cases name one item each, and the last case `_` fits any other string, so every other item costs 0.
